question: Which offices of a union may send a document for signature in its name and to which recipients, what identity proof binds a signer (a platform account, a verified e-mail address, a provider authentication) to the person whose name the audit trail states, what legal validity the union claims for a signature recorded in the platform or at a provider, and what makes the audit trail evidence (a sealed, verifiable record rather than an editable table)?
decision: Only officers or specifically delegated authorized signatories may send union documents for signature. Authenticate signer identity at an assurance level appropriate to document sensitivity (verified email alone is not conclusive identity proof), prevent any actor signing for another, bind the exact sealed document bytes, identity evidence and timestamps to a non-editable audit record, and retain provider certificate and verification method. Disable internal signing stub outside isolated tests. Legal effect is document- and jurisdiction-specific and must not be represented as guaranteed by DocuSign or by the platform.
originalProposedDecision: Only the org's officers and admins may send in the union's name. A signer must be a verified identity: a platform account or a provider-authenticated email; a sender can never sign for someone else. The platform claims no legal validity of its own; it relies on the provider (DocuSign) audit certificate. The internal stub is disabled outside test. The audit trail is append-only with the hash chain enforced.
independentApprovalScope: decision wording / platform baseline only; NOT independent security or operational testing
